findings.title: EBS volume not encrypted at rest
findings.description: An EBS volume is created without encryption enabled.
findings.risk: Data at rest is not protected. Physical access to storage media could lead to data exposure.

remediation.explanation: The EBS volume is created without the "encrypted = true" attribute. Data stored on this volume is not encrypted at rest.
remediation.impact: If the underlying storage media is compromised (e.g., through physical access, snapshot sharing, or AWS infrastructure incidents), data can be read without decryption keys.
remediation.remediation: Add "encrypted = true" to the EBS volume resource. Optionally specify a KMS key ID for customer-managed encryption.

autoFix.diff:
# Add the following line inside the resource block:
+ encrypted = true
assumptions: The attribute "encrypted" should be set to true for EBS volume encryption at rest
This fix does not modify any existing attributes
You should verify this value matches your organization's security policy

frameworks.reason: Unencrypted EBS volumes violate CIS 2.2.1 which requires EBS volume encryption to be enabled to protect data at rest.
Cryptographic Protection control requires encryption of data at rest; unencrypted EBS volumes violate this requirement.

findings.title: Unrestricted SSH access (Port 22 open to the world)
findings.description: A Security Group allows inbound SSH traffic (port 22) from any IP address (0.0.0.0/0).
findings.risk: Exposes servers to brute-force attacks from the public internet.

remediation.explanation: The security group ingress rule allows SSH (port 22) traffic from any IP address on the internet (0.0.0.0/0). This means anyone, anywhere can attempt to connect to your servers via SSH.
remediation.impact: Attackers can perform brute-force password attacks, exploit SSH vulnerabilities, or attempt to gain unauthorized access to your servers. This is one of the most common attack vectors in cloud environments.
remediation.remediation: Restrict the cidr_blocks for port 22 to your specific corporate IP address, VPN CIDR range, or a trusted bastion host IP. Never use 0.0.0.0/0 for administrative ports.

autoFix.description: Replace public CIDR "0.0.0.0/0" with a restricted range
assumptions: The current CIDR "0.0.0.0/0" is overly permissive for SSH access (port 22)
<YOUR_CORPORATE_CIDR> is a placeholder - you must replace it with your actual corporate IP or VPC CIDR
This fix assumes you have a known, trusted IP range to restrict access to

frameworks.reason: Unrestricted SSH access (port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0) directly violates CIS 5.2 which prohibits security groups from allowing ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports.
Exploit Public-Facing Application - Exposed SSH ports enable brute-force attacks and exploitation of public-facing services.

findings.title: S3 bucket configured for public read access
findings.description: An S3 bucket is configured with acl = "public-read" or "public-read-write".
findings.risk: Anyone on the internet can read the contents of the bucket, potentially leading to data leaks.

remediation.explanation: The S3 bucket has an ACL set to "public-read" or "public-read-write", granting read (and possibly write) access to anyone on the internet.
remediation.impact: Data stored in the bucket is publicly accessible. This can lead to data breaches, regulatory fines (GDPR, HIPAA), reputational damage, and potential legal liability.
remediation.remediation: Remove the acl attribute entirely. Use aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block to explicitly block public access. If public access is required, use a bucket policy with strict conditions instead.

autoFix.diff:
- acl = "public-read"
+ # acl attribute removed - use aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block instead
assumptions: The current ACL grants public access which is insecure for S3 bucket data protection
Public access should be controlled via aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block
You should verify your application does not require public read access before removing

frameworks.reason: Public-read ACLs on S3 buckets directly violate CIS 2.1.1 which requires S3 bucket policies to be secure and not grant public access.
Data from Cloud Storage Object - Public S3 buckets enable attackers to exfiltrate data directly from cloud storage.

findings.title: S3 bucket missing server-side encryption
findings.description: An S3 bucket does not have server_side_encryption_configuration defined.
findings.risk: Data stored in the bucket is not encrypted at rest, violating compliance standards.

remediation.explanation: Add a server_side_encryption_configuration block with AES256 or aws:kms.
remediation.impact: Add a server_side_encryption_configuration block with AES256 or aws:kms.
remediation.remediation: Add a server_side_encryption_configuration block with AES256 or aws:kms.
remediation.secureExample: Add a server_side_encryption_configuration block with AES256 or aws:kms.

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: An RDS database instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true.
findings.risk: Database is accessible from the public internet, drastically increasing the attack surface.

remediation.explanation: Set publicly_accessible = false to ensure the database is only accessible from within the VPC.
remediation.impact: Set publicly_accessible = false to ensure the database is only accessible from within the VPC.
remediation.remediation: Set publicly_accessible = false to ensure the database is only accessible from within the VPC.
remediation.secureExample: Set publicly_accessible = false to ensure the database is only accessible from within the VPC.

findings.title: RDS instance storage not encrypted
findings.description: An RDS database instance does not have storage encryption enabled.
findings.risk: Data at rest in the database is not encrypted, violating compliance standards.

remediation.explanation: The RDS instance does not have "storage_encrypted = true" set. Database data, backups, and logs are stored unencrypted.
remediation.impact: Database contents are vulnerable if storage media is compromised. This violates compliance requirements (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC 2) and exposes sensitive data.
remediation.remediation: Add "storage_encrypted = true" to the RDS instance. Note: Encryption can only be enabled at creation time - existing instances must be migrated.
remediation.secureExample:
resource "aws_db_instance" "secure" {
  identifier           = "secure-db"
  engine               = "postgres"
  instance_class       = "db.t3.micro"
  storage_encrypted    = true
  # kms_key_id        = "arn:aws:kms:..."  # Optional: customer-managed key
}

autoFix.diff:
# Add the following line inside the resource block:
+ storage_encrypted = true
assumptions: The attribute "storage_encrypted" should be set to true for RDS storage encryption
This fix does not modify any existing attributes
You should verify this value matches your organization's security policy

frameworks.reason: Unencrypted RDS storage violates CIS 2.3.1 which requires RDS instances to have encryption enabled.
Cryptographic Protection control requires encryption of data at rest; unencrypted RDS storage violates this requirement.

findings.title: RDS instance deletion protection disabled
findings.description: An RDS database instance has deletion_protection set to false or omitted.
findings.risk: The database can be accidentally or maliciously deleted, leading to data loss and downtime.

remediation.explanation: Set deletion_protection = true for production databases.
remediation.impact: Set deletion_protection = true for production databases.
remediation.remediation: Set deletion_protection = true for production databases.
remediation.secureExample: Set deletion_protection = true for production databases.

findings.title: Hardcoded secret detected in configuration
findings.description: A sensitive attribute (e.g., password, secret_key, api_key, token) is assigned a literal string value instead of a variable reference.
findings.risk: Hardcoded secrets can be exposed in version control, leading to credential compromise.

remediation.explanation: A sensitive attribute is assigned a literal string value instead of a variable reference.
remediation.impact: Hardcoded secrets can be exposed in version control, leading to credential compromise and unauthorized access.
remediation.remediation: Use Terraform variables (var.name), data sources, or a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) to inject sensitive values.

frameworks.reason: Authenticator Management control requires that secrets be managed securely; hardcoded credentials in IaC violate this.
Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files - Hardcoded secrets in Terraform files enable credential theft via source code exposure.
